newsitem.title: UK: Oxford to hold postal ballot on business school.
newsitem.headline: Oxford to hold postal ballot on business school.

text.p: A controversial proposal to build a business school at Oxford University will be decided by a postal ballot of teachers and staff, the University said in a statement on Monday.

Some 3,200 Oxford dons, senior library and administrative staff are to be allowed to decide on whether to accept a 20 million pound ($33 million) gift for the business school from a Syrian-born financier.

Last week a congregation of Oxford dons voted 259 to 214 against accepting the money from Wafic Said, a businessman who made his fortune in the construction boom in Saudi Arabia in the 1970s and 1980s.
Said announced the donation, the biggest single gift to Oxford University in 50 years, in July.
The University's executive council said it would "redouble its efforts" to find an alternative site for the new business school, acceptable to both the university and Said.

Some of those voting against the proposal in the first ballot expressed concern that the location of the new school, on a sports ground, contravened an agreement the University had undertaken to keep the site free of construction.
In order for a review of a possible new site to be carried out, the postal vote is to be delayed until next year.
